damit, als mit ihrem Eigenthum gebahren
selbige verkaufen, vertauschen, verschenken
können, mögen und sollen für ein.

men, welche die Gemeinden jetzt nun anlegen
wollen, wenn diese aber in Zukunft verkauft
werden, so wird davon das Laudemium 10 procent

auf Weite von 4 Meilen hin und rückweg
zu leisten.

selben
selben das Patronat-Recht über die Betscher

Zukunft erhöhet werden sollten, keine Vergü¬

gen für sich und Höchstdero Erben und Nach¬

co
co gesendet.

dorfgemeinden dem Einwande der Verletzung

nen Grundstücke und Gerechtigkeiten um das Dop¬

Contracte freystehen würde.

1, der Fürstlich Hohenlohe-Ingelfingensche General = Bevollmächtigte Baurath Glenk, welchem Sr. Hochfürstlichen Durchlauchten den Herrn Kriegs- und Forstrath von Triebenfeld Erbherrn auf Schweinerne und Kontopp als Höchst Ihren Freund und Beystand zugeordnet haben.

2, der Bürger und Stadtrepresentant Matheus Młynkiewicz als Bevollmächtigter der Betscher Bürgerschaft,

3, der Freyschulze Johann Chmara aus Stalluhn als Bevollmächtigter der Dorfgemeinden Stalluhn, Kulligowo, Schartzig, Stocki, Schwiechodzyn, Lowin

mit dem Antrage einen Contract zwischen Sr Hochfürstlichen Durchlauchten den Herrn regierenden Fürsten Friedrich Ludwig zu Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen der Bürgerschaft zu Betsche und den vorstehend benannten Dorfgemeinden auf den Grund der Punctation de dato Alt Schartzig den 16ten Julii 1804. aufzunehmen. Der Fürstlich Hohenlohesche Bevollmächtigte der Baurath Johann Wilhelm Glenk producirt die General-Vollmacht des Herrn Fürsten zu Hohenlohe vom 26ten April 1803. wornach derselbe authorisirt ist, Vorträge gültigerweise abzuschließen, von welcher Vollmacht eine vidimirte Abschrift zu diesen Acten genommen wurde.

Gleichergestalt überreicht auch der Młynkiewicz eine gerichtliche Vollmacht vom 5ten April 1804. nach welcher er authorisirt ist in Nahmen der Stadt mit dem Herrn regierenden Fürsten zu

zu Hohenlohe Durchlauchten einen Contract über sämtliche zur Herrschaft Betsche gehörige Grundstücke und nutzbare Gerechtigkeiten abzu schließen.

Ebenfalls überreicht der Chmara eine gerichtliche Vollmacht vom 5ten April 1804. wornach er von den Gemeinden Stalluhn, Kulligowo, Schartzig, Stoki, Schwiechoczyn, Lowin, gleichergestellt wie der Młynkiewicz authorisirt ist, einen Contract abzuschließen. Nach wechselseitig gepflogenen Unterhandlungen und nachdem die Punctation vom 16ten Julii 1804. beigebracht worden war, und die persöhnliche Tüchtigkeit der Comparenten Verträge zu schließen, keinem Bedenken unterworfen war so wurde der Contract, wie folget, aufgenommen.

§ 1.

§. 1. Es überlaßen Sr Hochfürstlichen Durchlaucht der Herr regierende Fürst Friedrich Ludwig zu Hohenlohe Ingelfingen, Gouverneur zu Breslau, General Inspecteur der Infanterie und Ritter der Königlichen Preußischen großen Orden als Erbherrn der Herrschaft Betsche in Meseritzer Kreyse belegen, an die Bürgerschaft der Stadt. Betsche und die Einwohner der Dörfer Kulligowo, Stalluhn, Schärtzig, Stoki, Schwichodczyn, Lowin, sämtliche ihnen zugehörige Vorwerke, Aecker Gärte, Wiesen, Brüche, Seen, Teiche, Teich stätte, Flüße, Hütung, Heyden, Läden, Forsten, Wälder, Büsche, Gesträuche, Geld und Natural-Zinsen, die Propination, Brau und Brennereÿe Gerechtigkeit, Ziegel und Kalkbrennereyen, das Obrn Vorwerk, kurz alle und jede nutzbare Rechte und Gerechtigkeiten, welche des Herrn Fürsten v Hohenlohe

Durchlauchten, zeithero als Eigenthümer benutzt und genoßen auch genießen können, mögen und sollen, in Pausch und Bogen, wie sie nur Nahmen haben mögen, insbesondere auch das Vorkaufsrecht auf die zu Erbzinsrechten verliehenen Scholtisseyn und Vorwerke, ausgenommen die Jurisdiction und die Laudemium, die Jagd, als welche sich Sr Hochfürstl. Durchlauchten als Obereigenthümer und beständiger Grundherr von Betsche für Sich und Höchst dero Nachfolger vorbehalten, zu ihrem wahren Erb- und Eigenthum der gestalt und also, daß die gedachte Stadt-Commune Betsche und die erwähnten Ortschaften damit, als mit ihrem Eigenthum gebahren selbige verkaufen, vertauschen, verschenken können, mögen und sollen für ein.

§ 2.

§ 2. wohl verabredetes Kauf und Erbstands - Quantum von Einmalhundert und Achtzigtausend Reichsthaler im Königlichen Preußischen Courant nach dem Müntzfuße von 1764. und einen jährlichen Grundzins von Eintausend Reichsthaler in Courant nach gleichem Müntzfuße.

§ 3. Mit der Bezahlung des Kauf- und Erbstands quanti wird es in der Art gehalten:

Es übernehmen die Stadt- und übrigen Dorf Gemeinden ad rationes protii nachstehend benannte, auf die Herrschaft Betsche in dem Hypothequenbuch der Königlichen Regierung zu Posen inta belirte Hypothequen-Schulden als

1, 48,000 rt für den Baurath Glenk eingetragen, von welcher Summe

36,000 rtt an den Banquieur Salomon Natan

Nathan junior zu Berlin und 12000 rtl. an den Banquier Meyer Bernhard zu Frankfurth a/o cedirt sind

2, 2000 rt. welche für den Handelsmann Abraham Moses Hirchel zu Breslau ein getragen sind

3, 5000 rt. welche für den Freyherrn von der Marwitz auf Rudnik intabulirt und an den Banquiens Meyer Bernhard in Frankfurth a/o cedirt sind

4, 5000 rthl. welche für die verwittwete Ober Amts-Räthin Christiane Dorothea Michaelis gebohrnen Eichborn intubulirt sind

5, 5000 rt. welche für den Baurath Johann Wil

helm Glenk intabulirt sind, und von ihm an den Banquieur Meyer Bernhard in Frankfurth cedirt worden, welche sämtliche Posten von 2 bis 5 von den Creditoren bereits gekündigt, und zu Weynachten c. a. zahlbar sind. Wobey bemerkt wird, daß die Zinsen der 48,000 rtl. bis zum 2ten Juli an: von den übrigen Capitalien aber bis zum 26ten Juli c. berichtigt sind.

6, 72,000 Rthl. welche für den Banquier Meyer Bernhard zu Frankfurth a/o bereits intabulirt, und die Zinsen à 5 procent bis zum 26ten Juli d. J. so wie bey den übrigen Capitalien berichtigt sind, und versprochen sie diese Summe an die Creditores zu berichtigen und sich darüber mit ihnen zu einigen

137,000 Rthl

7, stipuliren die Deputirten von dem Ueberrest des Kauf- und Erbstands quanti fünf und dreißig tausend Reichsthaler sofort an Sr Hochfürstl. Durchlaucht nach Breslau franco zu berichtigen, den Rest von 8000 rttl. aber Termino Johannis k. J. nebst 5 procent Zinsen ohnfehlbar zu berichtigen, wenn gehöriger Zeit gekündiget wird. Die vorstehend erwähnten 35000 rtlr. werden in der Art bezalt, Morgen des Tages den 29ten Julii 1000 rtl. von Morgen über 8. tage, wurde hat die übrigen 28000 rt. bezalt und zwar werden die 7000 rtl. franco nach Breslau auf Kosten der Zahlenden gesendet. Wenn

137000 rt Wenn unter den zu zalenden Geldern wichtige holländische Rand Ducaten sind, so werden diese mit 4 gg. Agio pro # angenommen. Sollten die Gemeinden morgen über 8 Tage als den 5ten August die 28000 rthl nicht bezalen, so hört der ganze heut geschloßene Contract auf und die Gemeinden sind verbunden die causirten Kosten zu bezalen, erhalten die 7000 rtl. jedoch ohne Zinsen wider zurück.

§. 4. Die Uebergabe erfolgt sogleich als die 28000 rtl. welche den 5ten August gezalt werden sollen, bezahlt sind. Da jedoch der ehemalige Pächter Bornstaedt noch in dem Besitz des hiesigen Vorwerks ist, und über deßen Exmission ein Prozeß anhängig ist, so bestehen die

Gemeinde zwar nicht darauf, daß ihnen der Besitz des Vorwerks sofort eingeräumt werde, wollen sich vielmehr gefallen laßen, daß bis das Exmissions-Urtheil nicht rechtskräftig ist, er darinnen bleiben und erst wenn das Exmissions Urthel rechtskräftig ist, exmittirt werden jedoch soll den Gemeinden dafür eine der Sache angemeßene billige und zweckmäßige Entschädigung von dem Herrn Fürsten Durchlauchten gegeben werde. Was hingegen die Forsten anbetrift, so sollen dieselben sogleich geschloßen seyn so wie sie es jetzt schon sind, und das darin geschlagene Holz, insofern es nicht zur Wirthschaft geschlagen ist, bleibt Eigenthum Sr. Durchlaucht des Herrn Fürsten v Hohenlohe Ingelfingen.

§. 5. Sämtliche herrschaftliche Wohn-, Wirthschaft

Forst und sonstige Gebäude sind den Gemeinden gleich als erb und eigenthümlich überlaßen, jedoch sind die Gemeinden verbunden den Förstern in den Försterhäusern in einer Stube die Wohnung bis zu Michaelis c. a. zu belaßen, so wie auf die Benutzung ihrer Gärten. Auch behalten sich Sr Durchlaucht das Schloß zum Sitze des Gerichts, der Wohnung des Gerichtsdieners, und der Wohnung für Höchstdieselben oder ihre Commissarien, auch eine Stallung zu 2. Pferden vor, welche sie selbst in baulichen Zustande unter behalten. Bey Bauten an diesem Gebäude sind die Gemeinden verbunden, dem Herrn Fürsten v Hohenlohe Ingelfingen Durchlauchten und ihren Nachfolgern die Ziegeln um den Kostenpreis abzulaßen und das Holz zum Ausbau aus der Heide unentgeldlich zu verabfolgen. Auch sind

die Gemeinden verbunden, das zur Heitzung der Gerichtsstube und des Gerichtsdieners nöthige Holz unentgeldlich aus der Forst zu verabreichen und heranzufahren. Gleichergestalt sind auch die Gemeinden verbunden, wenn Sr. Hochfürstl. Durchlaucht oder deren Commissorien hier anwesend sind, das nöthige Brennholz unentgeldlich zu verabreichen und heranzufahren.

§. 6. Was die zwischen Sr Hochfürstlichen Durchlauch ten und einigen Kaufleuten geschloßene Holz Kauf - Contracte anbetrift, so versprechen Hochdieselben die Holzkäufer abzufinden, ohne daß die Gemeinden dazu irgend einen Beytrag leisten.

§. 7. Es verpflichten sich die Eingangs erwähnte Stadt und dorfgemeinden bey Veräußerungen ihre

Grundstücke 10 Procent Laudemium an Sr. Hochfürstl. Durchlauchten und deren Nachfolger im Besitze von der Kaufs-Summe zu entrichten. Von diesen Laudemien sind jedoch die Stellen ausgenommen, welche die Gemeinden jetzt nun anlegen wollen, wenn diese aber in Zukunft verkauft werden, so wird davon das Laudemium 10 procent gleichfalls entrichtet.

§. 8. Ferner behalten sich Sr. Hochfürstlichen Durchlaucht vor, daß wenn sie höchstselbst oder deren Nachfolger im Besitze hierher kommen, oder ihre Commissarien hierher senden sollten, die Gemeinden schuldig sind die Vorspann führen auf Weite von 4 Meilen hin und rückweg zu leisten.

§. 9. Ferner behalten sich Sr. Durchlaucht, wenn die

selben das Patronat-Recht über die Betscher Kirche erhalten sollten, das Patronat Recht vor, jedoch sollen die Stadt und dorfgemeinden das Recht haben, den Geistlichen zu wählen, und denselben in Vorschlag zu bringen, welchen vorgeschlagenen Geistlichen Sr. Hochfürstl. Durchlaucht dem bischöflichen Consistorio zu praesentiren.

§. 10. versprechen.

Die Prozeße zwischen der Gemeinde zu Stocki und dem Herrn Fürsten v Hohenlohe wegen Ei genthums des Stocker Bruchs zwischen dem Herrn Fürsten v Hohenlohe und dem Besitzer von Zilomyśl[?] wegen des Einlaßungsrechtes, und zwischen dem Landrath v Schmaeling als Besitzer des Vorwerts in Glożewo, und dem Herrn Fürsten v Hohenlohe Durchlauchten, wegen Confirmation des Privilegii, so wie auch der

Prozeß zwischen dem Herrn Fürsten v Hohenlohe und dem Hertzig in Lowino, wegen Zurückgabe der Szalestwo, übernehmen die Gemeinden auf ihre Gefahr und Kosten und was sie ver streiter, oder im Wege des Vergleichs erhalten möchten, fällt den Gemeinden zu, ohne daß Sr. Durchlaucht daran den mindesten Anspruch haben.

§. 11. Die von Sr. Durchlaucht als Dominio von Betsche zeither entrichteten Competenz- Steuern und andere öffentliche und sonstige Abgaben, wenn(5) sie(6) Nahmen(7) haben(8) und(2) (3) Kosten(4), wohin auch die Krankenfuhren in das Schiller und Puncten Hauländer gehören, so wie auch die Fuhren zur Herbeÿholung und Abfahrt des Gerichts und wie sie sonst Nahmen haben, übernehmen die erwähnten Stadt und Dorfgemeinden und können die Letztern, wenn diese Abgaben an

Zukunft erhöhet werden sollten, keine Vergütigung von dem Herrn Fürsten v Hohenlohe Durchlaucht fordern, auch übernehmen die Gemeinden den von

Sr. Hochfürstlichen Durchlaucht zur hiesigen Stadtschule auf 1 Jahre zu leisten versprochenen Beytrag von 50 rthl.

§ 12. Beyde contrahirende Theile verpflichten sich diesen Contract bey den competenten Behörden zu verlaut laren und die Confirmation nachzusuchen, und machen sich Hochfürstlichen Durchlauchten hierbey verbund sich bestmöglichst zu verwenden, daß dieser Contract von den competenten Behörden confirmirt auch den Gemeinden der Consens zur fernerweiten Dismembration der ihnen überlaßenen und seite ertheilt werde.

§. 13. Sobald die Tradition des hiesigen Obra Vorwerks

erfolgt, wird den Stadt und dorfgemeinden zu gleich dasjenige Vieh und Wirthschafts Inventorium als welches unter dem Kauf und Erbstands quanto mit verkauft ist, in der Zahl übergeben, als der Pächter v Bornstaedt selbiges im Jahre 1800 bey der Uebergabe erhalten hat.

§. 14. Dieser Contract soll für Sr. Hochfürstlichen Durchlauchten den Herrn Fürsten zu Hohenlohe Ingelfingen für sich und Höchstdero Erben und Nachfolger, so wie auch von Seiten der Stadt und dorfgemeinden zu ewigen Zeiten verbindlich seyn. Und wird der jährliche zu bezahlende Canon oder Grundzins von 1000 rtl. in halbjährigen ratio mit 500 rtl. nehmlich jedesmal Termino Weynachten und Termino Johannis Babtistae alljährlich sub paena Executioni entrichtet, und nach Breslau franco

co gesendet.

§. 15. Solange die Gemeinden die ihnen überlaßene Grundstücke und Gerechtigkeiten nicht veränßern oder dismembiren, so bleibt der statupossivus in dem jetzigen Zustande Sobald aber das Vorwerk dismembrirt ist, sind die Erbkäufer schuldig, die intabelirten Posten auf Grundstücke transferiren und auf den Nahmen Sr. Hochfürstl. Durchlaucht löschen zu laßen

§. 16. Für den stipulirten Canon der 1000 rtl jährlich haften, sämtliche Gemeinden in solidum und laßen fus den Eintragung im Hypothoquen-Buche auf ihre Grundstücke gefallen, so wie hingegen auch Sr. Hochfürstl. Durchlaucht sich gefallen laßen, daß dieser gegenwärtige Contract

bey dem Hypothequer-Buche des Dominii Betsche und Zubehör eingetragen werde.

§. 17. Schließlich entsagen Controhentes allen und jeden Einwendungen, sie mögen Nahmen haben, wie sie wollen, insbesondere entsagen die Stadt und dorfgemeinden dem Einwande der Verletzung über die Hälfte, welcher ihnen dahin erklärt wurde, daß wenn das verabredete Kauf und Ein standt quantum den wahren Werth der überlaße nen Grundstücke und Gerechtigkeiten um das Doppelte übersteige, ihnen der Rücktritt von dem Contracte freystehen würde.

§. 18. Sr. Hochfürstl. Durchlauchten behalten sich die Oberaufsicht über die Forsten vor, welche sie dem Königlichen Oberförster Feller übertragen werden und die Gemeinden verpflichten sich diesen we

gen seiner Bemühungen zu entschädigen und sich dieserhalb mit ihm zu einigen.

No. 92.

We, the Princely Hohenloh-Ingelfingen Court-Office of the Lordship of Betsche, hereby make known and declare to all and sundry, but especially where it is needful, to be known, that there appeared before Us:

1, the Princely Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen Director of Estates and General Plenipotentiary, Building Councillor Johann Wilhelm Glenk, on the one part,

2, likewise the plenipotentiaries of the town and rural communities, namely of the town of Betsche, the villages of Staluhn, Schartzig, Schwichodizyn, Stocki, Lowin and Kulligowo,

a, the burgher and town representative Matheus Młynkiewicz

b) the free village headman Johann Chmara, and have concluded a hereditary-lease contract over the estates of the Lordship of Betsche, as

the negotiation of the 28th of July of this year, as also the supplement of the 29th of July of this year, sets forth more fully, reading thus: Actum Betsche, the 28th of July 1804. There appeared

1, the Princely Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen General Plenipotentiary, Building Councillor Glenk, to whom His Most Serene Highness has assigned the Councillor of War and Forests von Triebenfeld, hereditary lord of Schweinerne and Kontopp, as His Most High friend and assistant.

2, the burgher and town representative Matheus Młynkiewicz as plenipotentiary of the burghership of Betsche,

3, the free village headman Johann Chmara of Stalluhn as plenipotentiary of the village communities of Stalluhn, Kulligowo, Schartzig, Stocki, Schwiechodzyn, Lowin

with the motion to record a contract between His Most Serene Highness the reigning Prince Friedrich Ludwig zu Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen, the burghership of Betsche and the village communities named above, on the basis of the punctation dated Alt Schartzig, the 16th of July 1804. The Princely Hohenlohe plenipotentiary, the Building Councillor Johann Wilhelm Glenk, produces the general power of attorney of the Prince zu Hohenlohe of the 26th of April 1803, according to which he is authorised to conclude agreements in valid form; of which power of attorney a vidimated copy was taken to these records.

In like manner the said Młynkiewicz also presents a judicially executed power of attorney of the 5th of April 1804, according to which he is authorised, in the name of the town, to conclude with the reigning Prince

zu Hohenlohe, Serene Highness, a contract over all the parcels of land and profitable rights belonging to the Lordship of Betsche.

Likewise the said Chmara presents a judicially executed power of attorney of the 5th of April 1804, according to which he is authorised by the communities of Stalluhn, Kulligowo, Schartzig, Stoki, Schwiechoczyn, Lowin, on the same footing as the said Młynkiewicz, to conclude a contract. After negotiations conducted on both sides, and after the punctation of the 16th of July 1804 had been produced, and the personal capacity of the parties appearing to conclude contracts was subject to no doubt, the contract was recorded as follows.

§ 1.

§ 1. His Most Serene Highness the reigning Prince Friedrich Ludwig zu Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen, Governor of Breslau, General Inspector of the Infantry and Knight of the Royal Prussian great Orders, as hereditary lord of the Lordship of Betsche situated in the Meseritz district, makes over to the burghership of the town of Betsche and the inhabitants of the villages of Kulligowo, Stalluhn, Schärtzig, Stoki, Schwichodczyn, Lowin, all the demesne farms belonging to them, fields, gardens, meadows, marshes, lakes, ponds, pond-sites, rivers, pasturage, heaths, [uncertain: shops], forests, woods, thickets, scrub, money and natural rents, the propination rights, the brewing and distilling rights, brick- and lime-kilns, the Obra demesne farm, in short each and every profitable right and prerogative which the Prince von Hohenlohe,

Serene Highness, has hitherto as proprietor used and enjoyed and also can, may and shall enjoy, in Pausch und Bogen, by whatever names they may be called, and in particular also the right of pre-emption over the Scholtiseys and demesne farms granted out at hereditary quit-rent tenure - excepting the jurisdiction and the Laudemium, and the hunt, which His Most Serene Highness reserves to Himself and His Most High successors as supreme proprietor and perpetual ground-lord of Betsche - as their true hereditary property and possession, in such form and manner that the said town commune of Betsche and the aforementioned villages may deal therewith as with their own property, may sell, exchange, give it away, can, may and shall, for a

§ 2.

§ 2. duly agreed purchase and hereditary-tenure sum of one hundred and eighty thousand Reichsthaler in Royal Prussian Courant according to the coinage standard of 1764, and an annual ground-rent of one thousand Reichsthaler in Courant according to the same coinage standard.

§ 3. With regard to the payment of the purchase and hereditary-tenure sum, the matter is arranged in this manner:

The town and the remaining village communities take over, ad rationes protii, the following-named mortgage debts intabulated against the Lordship of Betsche in the mortgage book of the Royal Government at Posen, namely

1, 48,000 rt entered for the Building Councillor Glenk, of which sum

36,000 rtt have been ceded to the banker Salomon Natan

Nathan junior at Berlin, and 12000 rtl. to the banker Meyer Bernhard at Frankfurth a/O

2, 2000 rt. which are entered for the merchant Abraham Moses Hirchel at Breslau

3, 5000 rt. which are intabulated for the Baron von der Marwitz of Rudnik and have been ceded to the banker Meyer Bernhard at Frankfurth a/O

4, 5000 rthl. which are intabulated for the widowed Chief Bailiff's Lady Christiane Dorothea Michaelis, née Eichborn

5, 5000 rt. which are intabulated for the Building Councillor Johann Wil-

helm Glenk, and have been ceded by him to the banker Meyer Bernhard at Frankfurth, all which items from 2 to 5 have already been called in by the creditors and are payable at Christmas of this year. Whereby it is noted that the interest on the 48,000 rtl. has been settled up to the 2nd of July, but on the remaining capitals up to the 26th of July of this year.

6, 72,000 Rthl. which are already intabulated for the banker Meyer Bernhard at Frankfurth a/O, and the interest at 5 per cent settled up to the 26th of July of this year, as with the remaining capitals; and they promise to settle this sum with the creditors and to come to an agreement with them concerning it

137,000 Rthl

7, the deputies stipulate to settle immediately, out of the remainder of the purchase and hereditary-tenure sum, thirty-five thousand Reichsthaler to His Most Serene Highness at Breslau, carriage free, but the remainder of 8000 rttl. at the term of St John's next year, together with 5 per cent interest, without fail, if notice is given in due time. The above-mentioned 35000 rtlr. are to be paid in this manner: tomorrow, the 29th of July, 1000 rtl.; a week from tomorrow [uncertain: the remaining 28000 rt. are to be paid]; and namely the 7000 rtl. are to be sent carriage free to Breslau at the cost of the payers. If

137000 rt. If among the moneys to be paid there are heavy Dutch rim-ducats, these shall be accepted at 4 gg. agio per #. Should the communities not pay the 28000 rthl. a week from tomorrow, that is on the 5th of August, then the whole contract concluded this day lapses, and the communities are bound to pay the costs occasioned, but shall receive the 7000 rtl. back again, however without interest.

§ 4. The handing over follows as soon as the 28000 rtl., which are to be paid on the 5th of August, have been paid. Since, however, the former lessee Bornstaedt is still in possession of the demesne farm here, and a lawsuit is pending over his eviction, the

communities do not indeed insist that possession of the demesne farm be at once made over to them, but will rather be content that, so long as the eviction judgment is not final in law, he remain therein, and only when the eviction judgment is final in law shall he be evicted; however, for this the communities shall be given by the Prince, Serene Highness, a fair and appropriate compensation suited to the matter. As regards the forests, on the other hand, these shall be closed at once, as they already are now, and the timber felled therein, insofar as it has not been felled for the needs of the husbandry, remains the property of His Serene Highness the Prince von Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen.

§ 5. All the manorial dwelling-, farm-,

forest and other buildings are made over to the communities likewise as hereditary property; the communities are, however, bound to leave the foresters their dwelling in one room in the foresters' houses until Michaelmas of this year, as also the use of their gardens. His Serene Highness likewise reserves to himself the castle as the seat of the court, the dwelling of the court beadle, and a dwelling for His Most High Self or His commissaries, also a stabling for 2 horses, which they themselves maintain in good structural repair. In the case of building works on this edifice, the communities are bound to let the Prince von Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen, Serene Highness, and his successors have the bricks at cost price, and to deliver the timber for the construction free of charge from the heath. Also

the communities are bound to furnish and cart in, free of charge from the forest, the wood needed for heating the court room and the court beadle's [room]. In like manner the communities are also bound, when His Most Serene Highness or His commissaries are present here, to furnish and cart in the necessary firewood free of charge.

§ 6. As regards the timber purchase contracts concluded between His Most Serene Highness and certain merchants, His Most High Self promises to satisfy the timber purchasers without the communities making any contribution thereto.

§ 7. The town and village communities mentioned at the outset undertake, upon alienations of their

parcels of land, to render 10 per cent Laudemium on the purchase sum to His Most Serene Highness and his successors in possession. From these laudemia, however, those holdings are excepted which the communities now intend to lay out; but if these are sold in future, the Laudemium of 10 per cent is likewise to be rendered thereon.

§ 8. Further, His Most Serene Highness reserves that, when he himself or his successors in possession come hither, or should send their commissaries hither, the communities are bound to provide the relay teams for a distance of 4 miles, there and back.

§ 9. Further, His Serene Highness reserves, should he

obtain the right of patronage over the church at Betsche, the right of patronage; however, the town and village communities shall have the right to elect the clergyman and to put him forward in nomination, which nominated clergyman His Most Serene Highness [is] to present to the episcopal Consistory.

§ 10. promise.

The lawsuits between the community of Stocki and the Prince von Hohenlohe concerning ownership of the Stocki marsh; between the Prince von Hohenlohe and the possessor of Zilomyśl[?] concerning the right of admission [of cattle]; and between the Landrath von Schmaeling as possessor of the demesne farm in Glożewo and the Prince von Hohenlohe, Serene Highness, concerning confirmation of the privilege; as also the

lawsuit between the Prince von Hohenlohe and Hertzig in Lowino concerning the restitution of the Szalestwo, the communities take over at their own risk and cost, and whatever they may win in litigation, or obtain by way of settlement, falls to the communities, without His Serene Highness having the least claim thereto.

§ 11. The competence-taxes and other public and further dues hitherto paid by His Serene Highness as Dominium of Betsche, whatever(5) they(6) names(7) have(8) and(2) (3) costs(4), among which also belong the sick-transports into the Schiller and Puncten Hauländer, as also the carting for the fetching in and conveying away of the court, and by whatever other names they may be called, the said town and village communities take over; and the latter, should these dues in

future be increased, can demand no compensation from the Prince von Hohenlohe, Serene Highness; the communities also take over the contribution of 50 rthl. which His Most Serene Highness promised to render to the town school here for 1 year.

§ 12. Both contracting parties undertake to have this contract published before the competent authorities and to seek the confirmation, and His Most Serene Highness hereby binds himself to exert himself in the best way possible that this contract be confirmed by the competent authorities, and that the consent be granted to the communities for the further dismemberment of what has been made over to them and [text lost].

§ 13. As soon as the tradition of the Obra demesne farm here

takes place, there shall at the same time be handed over to the town and village communities the livestock and farm inventory - as being included in the sale under the purchase and entry sum - in the same number as the lessee von Bornstaedt received the same in the year 1800 upon the handing over.

§ 14. This contract shall be binding for His Most Serene Highness the Prince zu Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen for himself and His Most High heirs and successors, as also on the part of the town and village communities, for all time. And the annual canon or ground-rent of 1000 rtl. to be paid shall be rendered in half-yearly instalments of 500 rtl., namely each time at the term of Christmas and the term of St John the Baptist, yearly, sub paena Executioni, and sent carriage

free.

§ 15. So long as the communities do not alienate or dismember the parcels of land and rights made over to them, the status possivus remains in its present condition. But as soon as the demesne farm is dismembered, the hereditary purchasers are bound to have the intabulated items transferred onto the [several] parcels and cancelled as against the name of His Most Serene Highness.

§ 16. For the stipulated canon of 1000 rtl. yearly all the communities are liable in solidum, and consent to the entry thereof in the mortgage book against their parcels of land; just as, conversely, His Most Serene Highness consents that this present contract

be entered in the mortgage book of the Dominium of Betsche and its appurtenances.

§ 17. Finally, the Contrahentes renounce each and every objection, by whatever names they may be called; in particular the town and village communities renounce the objection of injury beyond the half, which was explained to them to this effect, that if the agreed purchase and entry sum exceeded the true value of the parcels of land and rights made over by double, they would be free to withdraw from the contract.

§ 18. His Most Serene Highness reserves to himself the superintendence over the costs, which he will entrust to the Royal Chief Forester Feller, and the communities undertake to indemnify him

for his pains and to come to an agreement with him thereon.

Thereupon, since nothing further was to be brought forward, the negotiation was closed, the protocol read out, interpreted by the sworn interpreter Eichaust to the deputies of the town and village communities who are not fully conversant with the German language and who had requested the keeping of a separate side-protocol in the Polish language, approved and signed; whereby it was further noted by the [uncertain: Contrahenten] that the costs of the recording, expedition, publication and confirmation are to be borne in halves by both parties. Read out, approved and

signed. Read myself and approved. Johann Wilhelm Glenk, Most Princely Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen General Plenipotentiary. Peter Friedrich August v Triebenfeld. Jan Chmara, as authorised representative. Mateusz Myłnkiewicz, authorised representative, plenipotentiary. Josef Echaust as interpreter. Metzig,

Justitiarius.

Neumann, Actuarius. Actum Betsche, the 29th of July 1804. To-day there appeared

1, the Princely Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen General Plenipotentiary, Building Councillor Johann Wilhelm Glenk; likewise the special plenipotentiary of the burghership, the said Matheus Myłnkie-

wicz; 3, the plenipotentiary of the communities of Kuligow, Stalluhn, Szartzig, Stoki, Schwichodzin, Lowin, [namely] Chmara, and bring forward the following in addition to the contract recorded yesterday:

§ 1. The Prince von Hohenlohe, Serene Highness, assures the communities that apart from the mortgage capitals already called in, none shall be called in within half a year.

§ 2. The town and village communities undertake to bear for ever, in the event of criminal investigations arising, the costs of investigation, insofar as the remaining communities belonging to the Betsche Schlüssel are not themselves bound to bear the same. Therewith the negotiation was closed, the protocol read out, [and] to the deputies of the community, who

are not entirely conversant with the German language [and] had requested the keeping of a protocol in the Polish language, interpreted by the sworn interpreter Echaust, approved and signed. Johann Wilhelm Glenk.

J. Chmara mpp

M. Młynkiewicz

Metzig

Neumann. Since now an authenticated engrossment is needful, and has been requested on that account, the present engrossment is issued in witness thereof under Our seal and signature.

Done at Betrche, the 7th of December 1804. Princely Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen Court-Office.

We, the Princely Hohenloh-Ingelfingen Court-Office of the Lordship of Betsche, hereby make known and declare to all and sundry, but especially where it is needful, to be known, that there appeared before Us:

1, the Princely Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen Director of Estates and General Plenipotentiary, Building Councillor Johann Wilhelm Glenk, on the one part,

2, likewise the plenipotentiaries of the town and rural communities, namely of the town of Betsche, the villages of Staluhn, Schartzig, Schwichodizyn, Stocki, Lowin and Kulligowo,

a, the burgher and town representative Matheus Młynkiewicz

b) the free village headman Johann Chmara, and have concluded a hereditary-lease contract over the estates of the Lordship of Betsche, as

the negotiation of the 28th of July of this year, as also the supplement of the 29th of July of this year, sets forth more fully, reading thus: Actum Betsche, the 28th of July 1804. There appeared

1, the Princely Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen General Plenipotentiary, Building Councillor Glenk, to whom His Most Serene Highness has assigned the Councillor of War and Forests von Triebenfeld, hereditary lord of Schweinerne and Kontopp, as His Most High friend and assistant.

2, the burgher and town representative Matheus Młynkiewicz as plenipotentiary of the burghership of Betsche,

3, the free village headman Johann Chmara of Stalluhn as plenipotentiary of the village communities of Stalluhn, Kulligowo, Schartzig, Stocki, Schwiechodzyn, Lowin

with the motion to record a contract between His Most Serene Highness the reigning Prince Friedrich Ludwig zu Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen, the burghership of Betsche and the village communities named above, on the basis of the punctation dated Alt Schartzig, the 16th of July 1804. The Princely Hohenlohe plenipotentiary, the Building Councillor Johann Wilhelm Glenk, produces the general power of attorney of the Prince zu Hohenlohe of the 26th of April 1803, according to which he is authorised to conclude agreements in valid form; of which power of attorney a vidimated copy was taken to these records.

In like manner the said Młynkiewicz also presents a judicially executed power of attorney of the 5th of April 1804, according to which he is authorised, in the name of the town, to conclude with the reigning Prince

zu Hohenlohe, Serene Highness, a contract over all the parcels of land and profitable rights belonging to the Lordship of Betsche.

Likewise the said Chmara presents a judicially executed power of attorney of the 5th of April 1804, according to which he is authorised by the communities of Stalluhn, Kulligowo, Schartzig, Stoki, Schwiechoczyn, Lowin, on the same footing as the said Młynkiewicz, to conclude a contract. After negotiations conducted on both sides, and after the punctation of the 16th of July 1804 had been produced, and the personal capacity of the parties appearing to conclude contracts was subject to no doubt, the contract was recorded as follows.

§ 1.

§ 1. His Most Serene Highness the reigning Prince Friedrich Ludwig zu Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen, Governor of Breslau, General Inspector of the Infantry and Knight of the Royal Prussian great Orders, as hereditary lord of the Lordship of Betsche situated in the Meseritz district, makes over to the burghership of the town of Betsche and the inhabitants of the villages of Kulligowo, Stalluhn, Schärtzig, Stoki, Schwichodczyn, Lowin, all the demesne farms belonging to them, fields, gardens, meadows, marshes, lakes, ponds, pond-sites, rivers, pasturage, heaths, [uncertain: shops], forests, woods, thickets, scrub, money and natural rents, the propination rights, the brewing and distilling rights, brick- and lime-kilns, the Obra demesne farm, in short each and every profitable right and prerogative which the Prince von Hohenlohe,

Serene Highness, has hitherto as proprietor used and enjoyed and also can, may and shall enjoy, in Pausch und Bogen, by whatever names they may be called, and in particular also the right of pre-emption over the Scholtiseys and demesne farms granted out at hereditary quit-rent tenure - excepting the jurisdiction and the Laudemium, and the hunt, which His Most Serene Highness reserves to Himself and His Most High successors as supreme proprietor and perpetual ground-lord of Betsche - as their true hereditary property and possession, in such form and manner that the said town commune of Betsche and the aforementioned villages may deal therewith as with their own property, may sell, exchange, give it away, can, may and shall, for a

§ 2.

§ 2. duly agreed purchase and hereditary-tenure sum of one hundred and eighty thousand Reichsthaler in Royal Prussian Courant according to the coinage standard of 1764, and an annual ground-rent of one thousand Reichsthaler in Courant according to the same coinage standard.

§ 3. With regard to the payment of the purchase and hereditary-tenure sum, the matter is arranged in this manner:

The town and the remaining village communities take over, ad rationes protii, the following-named mortgage debts intabulated against the Lordship of Betsche in the mortgage book of the Royal Government at Posen, namely

1, 48,000 rt entered for the Building Councillor Glenk, of which sum

36,000 rtt have been ceded to the banker Salomon Natan

Nathan junior at Berlin, and 12000 rtl. to the banker Meyer Bernhard at Frankfurth a/O

2, 2000 rt. which are entered for the merchant Abraham Moses Hirchel at Breslau

3, 5000 rt. which are intabulated for the Baron von der Marwitz of Rudnik and have been ceded to the banker Meyer Bernhard at Frankfurth a/O

4, 5000 rthl. which are intabulated for the widowed Chief Bailiff's Lady Christiane Dorothea Michaelis, née Eichborn

5, 5000 rt. which are intabulated for the Building Councillor Johann Wil-

helm Glenk, and have been ceded by him to the banker Meyer Bernhard at Frankfurth, all which items from 2 to 5 have already been called in by the creditors and are payable at Christmas of this year. Whereby it is noted that the interest on the 48,000 rtl. has been settled up to the 2nd of July, but on the remaining capitals up to the 26th of July of this year.

6, 72,000 Rthl. which are already intabulated for the banker Meyer Bernhard at Frankfurth a/O, and the interest at 5 per cent settled up to the 26th of July of this year, as with the remaining capitals; and they promise to settle this sum with the creditors and to come to an agreement with them concerning it

137,000 Rthl

7, the deputies stipulate to settle immediately, out of the remainder of the purchase and hereditary-tenure sum, thirty-five thousand Reichsthaler to His Most Serene Highness at Breslau, carriage free, but the remainder of 8000 rttl. at the term of St John's next year, together with 5 per cent interest, without fail, if notice is given in due time. The above-mentioned 35000 rtlr. are to be paid in this manner: tomorrow, the 29th of July, 1000 rtl.; a week from tomorrow [uncertain: the remaining 28000 rt. are to be paid]; and namely the 7000 rtl. are to be sent carriage free to Breslau at the cost of the payers. If

137000 rt. If among the moneys to be paid there are heavy Dutch rim-ducats, these shall be accepted at 4 gg. agio per #. Should the communities not pay the 28000 rthl. a week from tomorrow, that is on the 5th of August, then the whole contract concluded this day lapses, and the communities are bound to pay the costs occasioned, but shall receive the 7000 rtl. back again, however without interest.

§ 4. The handing over follows as soon as the 28000 rtl., which are to be paid on the 5th of August, have been paid. Since, however, the former lessee Bornstaedt is still in possession of the demesne farm here, and a lawsuit is pending over his eviction, the

communities do not indeed insist that possession of the demesne farm be at once made over to them, but will rather be content that, so long as the eviction judgment is not final in law, he remain therein, and only when the eviction judgment is final in law shall he be evicted; however, for this the communities shall be given by the Prince, Serene Highness, a fair and appropriate compensation suited to the matter. As regards the forests, on the other hand, these shall be closed at once, as they already are now, and the timber felled therein, insofar as it has not been felled for the needs of the husbandry, remains the property of His Serene Highness the Prince von Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen.

§ 5. All the manorial dwelling-, farm-,

forest and other buildings are made over to the communities likewise as hereditary property; the communities are, however, bound to leave the foresters their dwelling in one room in the foresters' houses until Michaelmas of this year, as also the use of their gardens. His Serene Highness likewise reserves to himself the castle as the seat of the court, the dwelling of the court beadle, and a dwelling for His Most High Self or His commissaries, also a stabling for 2 horses, which they themselves maintain in good structural repair. In the case of building works on this edifice, the communities are bound to let the Prince von Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen, Serene Highness, and his successors have the bricks at cost price, and to deliver the timber for the construction free of charge from the heath. Also

the communities are bound to furnish and cart in, free of charge from the forest, the wood needed for heating the court room and the court beadle's [room]. In like manner the communities are also bound, when His Most Serene Highness or His commissaries are present here, to furnish and cart in the necessary firewood free of charge.

§ 6. As regards the timber purchase contracts concluded between His Most Serene Highness and certain merchants, His Most High Self promises to satisfy the timber purchasers without the communities making any contribution thereto.

§ 7. The town and village communities mentioned at the outset undertake, upon alienations of their

parcels of land, to render 10 per cent Laudemium on the purchase sum to His Most Serene Highness and his successors in possession. From these laudemia, however, those holdings are excepted which the communities now intend to lay out; but if these are sold in future, the Laudemium of 10 per cent is likewise to be rendered thereon.

§ 8. Further, His Most Serene Highness reserves that, when he himself or his successors in possession come hither, or should send their commissaries hither, the communities are bound to provide the relay teams for a distance of 4 miles, there and back.

§ 9. Further, His Serene Highness reserves, should he

obtain the right of patronage over the church at Betsche, the right of patronage; however, the town and village communities shall have the right to elect the clergyman and to put him forward in nomination, which nominated clergyman His Most Serene Highness [is] to present to the episcopal Consistory.

§ 10. promise.

The lawsuits between the community of Stocki and the Prince von Hohenlohe concerning ownership of the Stocki marsh; between the Prince von Hohenlohe and the possessor of Zilomyśl[?] concerning the right of admission [of cattle]; and between the Landrath von Schmaeling as possessor of the demesne farm in Glożewo and the Prince von Hohenlohe, Serene Highness, concerning confirmation of the privilege; as also the

lawsuit between the Prince von Hohenlohe and Hertzig in Lowino concerning the restitution of the Szalestwo, the communities take over at their own risk and cost, and whatever they may win in litigation, or obtain by way of settlement, falls to the communities, without His Serene Highness having the least claim thereto.

§ 11. The competence-taxes and other public and further dues hitherto paid by His Serene Highness as Dominium of Betsche, whatever(5) they(6) names(7) have(8) and(2) (3) costs(4), among which also belong the sick-transports into the Schiller and Puncten Hauländer, as also the carting for the fetching in and conveying away of the court, and by whatever other names they may be called, the said town and village communities take over; and the latter, should these dues in

future be increased, can demand no compensation from the Prince von Hohenlohe, Serene Highness; the communities also take over the contribution of 50 rthl. which His Most Serene Highness promised to render to the town school here for 1 year.

§ 12. Both contracting parties undertake to have this contract published before the competent authorities and to seek the confirmation, and His Most Serene Highness hereby binds himself to exert himself in the best way possible that this contract be confirmed by the competent authorities, and that the consent be granted to the communities for the further dismemberment of what has been made over to them and [text lost].

§ 13. As soon as the tradition of the Obra demesne farm here

takes place, there shall at the same time be handed over to the town and village communities the livestock and farm inventory - as being included in the sale under the purchase and entry sum - in the same number as the lessee von Bornstaedt received the same in the year 1800 upon the handing over.

§ 14. This contract shall be binding for His Most Serene Highness the Prince zu Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen for himself and His Most High heirs and successors, as also on the part of the town and village communities, for all time. And the annual canon or ground-rent of 1000 rtl. to be paid shall be rendered in half-yearly instalments of 500 rtl., namely each time at the term of Christmas and the term of St John the Baptist, yearly, sub paena Executioni, and sent carriage

free.

§ 15. So long as the communities do not alienate or dismember the parcels of land and rights made over to them, the status possivus remains in its present condition. But as soon as the demesne farm is dismembered, the hereditary purchasers are bound to have the intabulated items transferred onto the [several] parcels and cancelled as against the name of His Most Serene Highness.

§ 16. For the stipulated canon of 1000 rtl. yearly all the communities are liable in solidum, and consent to the entry thereof in the mortgage book against their parcels of land; just as, conversely, His Most Serene Highness consents that this present contract

be entered in the mortgage book of the Dominium of Betsche and its appurtenances.

§ 17. Finally, the Contrahentes renounce each and every objection, by whatever names they may be called; in particular the town and village communities renounce the objection of injury beyond the half, which was explained to them to this effect, that if the agreed purchase and entry sum exceeded the true value of the parcels of land and rights made over by double, they would be free to withdraw from the contract.

§ 18. His Most Serene Highness reserves to himself the superintendence over the costs, which he will entrust to the Royal Chief Forester Feller, and the communities undertake to indemnify him

for his pains and to come to an agreement with him thereon.

Thereupon, since nothing further was to be brought forward, the negotiation was closed, the protocol read out, interpreted by the sworn interpreter Eichaust to the deputies of the town and village communities who are not fully conversant with the German language and who had requested the keeping of a separate side-protocol in the Polish language, approved and signed; whereby it was further noted by the [uncertain: Contrahenten] that the costs of the recording, expedition, publication and confirmation are to be borne in halves by both parties. Read out, approved and

signed. Read myself and approved. Johann Wilhelm Glenk, Most Princely Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen General Plenipotentiary. Peter Friedrich August v Triebenfeld. Jan Chmara, as authorised representative. Mateusz Myłnkiewicz, authorised representative, plenipotentiary. Josef Echaust as interpreter. Metzig,

Justitiarius.

Neumann, Actuarius. Actum Betsche, the 29th of July 1804. To-day there appeared

1, the Princely Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen General Plenipotentiary, Building Councillor Johann Wilhelm Glenk; likewise the special plenipotentiary of the burghership, the said Matheus Myłnkie-

wicz; 3, the plenipotentiary of the communities of Kuligow, Stalluhn, Szartzig, Stoki, Schwichodzin, Lowin, [namely] Chmara, and bring forward the following in addition to the contract recorded yesterday:

§ 1. The Prince von Hohenlohe, Serene Highness, assures the communities that apart from the mortgage capitals already called in, none shall be called in within half a year.

The town and village communities undertake to bear for ever, in the event of criminal investigations arising, the costs of investigation, insofar as the remaining communities belonging to the Betsche Schlüssel are not themselves bound to bear the same. summary_en: Hereditary-lease and sale of the whole lordship of Betsche by Prince Friedrich Ludwig of Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen, through his general attorney building councillor Johann Wilhelm Glenck, to the burgesses of Betsche and the villages of Stalluhn, Kulligowo, Schartzig, Stocki, Schwichodzyn and Lowin, represented by Matheus Młynkiewicz and Jan Chmara: 180,000 Rthl purchase sum plus 1,000 Rthl annual ground-rent, largely discharged by assuming 137,000 Rthl of intabulated mortgages. Reserved are jurisdiction, hunt, Laudemium, castle and forest supervision; a Polish interpreter, Echaust, attended. With royal confirmation of 1806.
summary_de: Erbpachtvertrag über die gesamte Herrschaft Betsche, den Bauinspektor bzw. Generalbevollmächtigter Johann Wilhelm Glenck für Friedrich Ludwig von Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen mit den Bevollmächtigten Matheus Młynkiewicz (Stadt Betsche) und Johann Chmara (Stalluhn, Kulligowo, Schartzig, Stoki, Schwichodzyn, Lowin) schloss: Übergabe aller Vorwerke, Wälder, Propinations- und Nutzungsrechte in Pausch und Bogen für 180.000 Rthl Kaufsumme, davon 137.000 Rthl übernommene Hypotheken, sowie 1000 Rthl jährlichen Canon; Jurisdiktion, Laudemium (10 %), Jagd und Forstaufsicht bleiben vorbehalten. Beigefügt Nachtragsprotokoll, polnische Unterschriften und die Kammerbestätigung.
